summary.text: Plant anatomy, also called phytotomy, is the study of the internal structure of plants.
It once included plant morphology, the description of a plant's outward form, but since the mid-20th century it has been a separate field.
It is now often investigated at the cellular level, and it often involves sectioning tissues and using microscopy.

items.prompt: Two students study one plant. One writes up its outward shape; the other looks inside at its cells. Which is doing plant anatomy as defined since the mid-20th century?

options.label: The one studying its internal structure
The one describing its physical outward form
Both, since the field covers outward form too
Neither, since the field only covers fossils

items.explain: Since the mid-20th century, plant anatomy refers only to internal structure, while outward form belongs to plant morphology.

items.prompt: In 1672 a British doctor and co-founder of plant anatomy published a book describing the tiny building blocks of plants, though he gave them strange names. What had he recognized?

options.label: The genes that pass traits between plants
The cells that make up plants
The fossils that record plant history
The hormones that steer plant growth

items.explain: Nehemiah Grew is credited with recognizing plant cells, though he called them 'vesicles' and 'bladders'.

items.prompt: Haberlandt grouped plant tissues into systems such as absorptive, mechanical and photosynthetic. What was his sorting principle?

options.label: By where a tissue sits on the plant's outside
By how old each tissue is
By what each tissue does
By which fossils it resembles

items.explain: Haberlandt classified plant tissue based upon function, and described twelve types of tissue systems.

items.prompt: After Darwin's Origin of Species, a Canadian botanist compared different vascular plant groups to build evolutionary lines. What did he use?

options.label: The colours of their flowers
The number of seeds each produced
The soils where they grew
The form and structure of plants

items.explain: Edward Charles Jeffrey applied Darwin's theory to plants, using their form and structure to establish a number of evolutionary lines.

items.prompt: In 1813 Augustin de Candolle argued that plant classification should rest on one thing only. Which?

options.label: How plants work inside
Plants' internal structure
Where plants grow
How tall plants get

items.explain: De Candolle argued that plant anatomy, not physiology, ought to be the sole basis for plant classification.

items.prompt: Under a microscope, a botanist finds a simple plant made of a single cell. By Schleiden's 1838 statement, what kind of plant is it?

options.label: A lower plant
A higher plant
Neither; all plants are many cells
It cannot be classified

items.explain: Schleiden stated that the lower plants all consist of one cell, while the higher plants are composed of many individual cells.
